backtest_protocol: docs/backtesting.md canonical three fixed windows. Core uses canonical snapshots; Space variants use exp-20260510-028 augmented Space snapshots. The accepted_before variant reproduces exp-20260512-112 policy semantics.
decision_rationale: Restricting the accepted watch-liquidity top-up by established TQS bucket did not clear the three-window gate versus exp-20260512-112. Keep the current all-TQS watch-liquidity helper and do not retry nearby TQS-scope splits on the same frozen snapshots without forward evidence.

gate1.known_bias: Space candidate snapshots are frozen historical replay copies built from a 2026-05-10 research universe. TQS and liquidity-tier metadata are production-observable in the shared Space sleeve, but any accepted change must remain default-off until forward evidence matures.

gate_questions.1_alpha_hypothesis: risk allocation: keep the accepted watch-liquidity scalar at 1.10x but test its established TQS bucket scope.

2_history_check.exp-20260512-004: Accepted perfect Space TQS bucket. This reuses that bucket definition for a helper-scope test.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-008: Accepted near-perfect Space trend TQS bucket. This reuses that bucket definition instead of creating an arbitrary threshold.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-112: Accepted liquidity_tier=watch 1.10x across all TQS buckets; this is the fixed before state.
2_history_check.exp-20260512-114_and_951: Rejected strategy-scope splits for watch liquidity.
2_history_check.exp-20260513-003: Rejected peer-state scope splits for watch liquidity.

gate_questions.3_single_causal_variable: space_watch_liquidity_tqs_scope. Candidate pool, scalar value, accepted Space stack, targets, stops, ranking, add-ons, LLM/news, and live slots stay fixed.
gate_questions.4_acceptance_standard: docs/backtesting.md three fixed windows; require positive aggregate EV/PnL versus exp-112, at least 2/3 improved EV windows, no EV-regressed window, max drawdown drift <= 0.5 pp, survival >= 5%, >=50 total trades, nonzero adjusted in-scope signals, and nonzero out-of-scope watch signals.

hypothesis: The accepted Space watch-liquidity scalar may be carried by particular signal-quality buckets. Since near-perfect/perfect TQS already define accepted Space quality ladders, scoping the existing watch-liquidity 1.10x helper by those buckets may improve replacement value without changing candidate pool, scalar value, ranking, exits, LLM/news, or live slots.
interpretation: Restricting the accepted watch-liquidity top-up by established TQS bucket did not clear the three-window gate versus exp-20260512-112. Keep the current all-TQS watch-liquidity helper and do not retry nearby TQS-scope splits on the same frozen snapshots without forward evidence.

llm_metrics.why_not_llm_soft_ranking: Space soft-ranking remains label-limited; this run uses deterministic production metadata already present in the observation slot.

next_evidence_needed: If rejected, do not retry nearby TQS-scope splits for the accepted watch-liquidity helper on these frozen snapshots. Future Space work should use forward replacement value or a new production-visible catalyst-quality field.
rejection_reason: Restricting the accepted watch-liquidity top-up by established TQS bucket did not clear the three-window gate versus exp-20260512-112. Keep the current all-TQS watch-liquidity helper and do not retry nearby TQS-scope splits on the same frozen snapshots without forward evidence.
single_causal_variable: TQS bucket scope for the accepted 1.10x watch-liquidity risk top-up
why_not_other_changes: LLM soft-ranking is data-limited; noisy ticker additions, broad defense-budget source scalars, primary-authority source scalars, contract-profile scalars, generic risk caps, strategy-scope splits, and peer-scope splits are already rejected. This tests one production-visible TQS-scope variable for an accepted helper.
